item.title: HackerPulse — November 5, 2025: Preloads, Borders as Software, and the Web’s Origins
item.description: Today’s episode surveys a diverse set of Hacker News stories: X now preloads and opens every tweet link in an in-app WebView, raising privacy and security questions. A case study on Iceland's border logistics reframes borders as software rules, with a resident model that forecasts immigration outcomes. Bud Smith’s Truck Desk and Xiao Xiao evoke maker culture and the Flash era’s art and licensing drama. A primer on manifolds shows how geometry underpins physics and data, while NoLongerEvil-Thermostat demonstrates DIY firmware hacking. The Morris worm review recalls the Web’s security infancy, followed by Show HN CSS terrain generators and pg_lake, which combines Postgres with Iceberg data lakes. Finally, Codemaps marks a new era of AI-annotated code navigation. A single episode about how code, culture, and constraints shape what we share, build, and protect online.

item.title: HackerPulse — October 19, 2025: DOS TUIs, Ripgrep 15.0, and the AMD Strix Halo
item.description: Today’s HackerPulse episode stitches together a curated set of Hacker News stories. We start with a nostalgic deep-dive into DOS-era full-screen TUIs—MS-DOS 5’s editor, SideKick Plus as a TSR, and the Borland Turbo family with integrated compilers and debuggers in tiny footprints—and compare that polish to modern IDEs, noting how LSP/BSP ecosystems like Doom Emacs, Neovim, and Helix are reviving TUI-driven workflows for SSH/tmux-style remote work. We also cover Ripgrep 15.0’s big release: broader platform support, speed wins, bug fixes, and feature enhancements for those who live in the terminal. The episode spotlights a few terse, aesthetic content bits like the naked link './watch' and Wageningen University’s Root System Drawings, then explores Neural Symphony—a tinnitus neuromodulation tool blending Steve Harrison’s sequences with myNoise’s engine for user-controlled masking sounds. We pivot to SQL anti-patterns and fixes, emphasizing design-for-queries and avoiding view-on-view traps. OpenMixerProject’s StageConnect shows Behringer’s A²B bridge to a Behringer/Midas workflow, while AMD’s Strix Halo details a dual Zen 5, high-end APU with a robust iGPU and massive bandwidth. A meditation on attention economics ties the thread together, followed by Free Programming Books—a community-driven hub of free resources and governance for open education. It’s a compact, thoughtful mix of nostalgia, practical tech insight, and a forward-looking view on how we code and learn in 2025.

item.title: HackerPulse Oct 18, 2025: Hetzner savings, governance shifts, and AI debates
item.description: In this episode dated October 18, 2025, HackerPulse surveys the day’s top stories: Digital Society slashes cloud bills by migrating from AWS and DigitalOcean to Hetzner, quadrupling capacity with Kubernetes, Talos Linux, CloudNativePG, Terraform, Helm, and GitHub Actions; Ruby core teams take ownership of RubyGems and Bundler; Ring teams with Flock to share doorbell footage with law enforcement, raising privacy and bias concerns; Karpathy frames AGI as a decade-long journey focused on agents rather than a single breakthrough; Claude Skills introduces a modular, on-demand tooling approach for AI tasks; Ofcom’s Online Safety Act and its potential extraterritorial reach; plus a practical primer on fact-checking to curb misinformation online.
